1	# Carbon-aware Compute Scheduling Market
2	
3	A backend service for a carbon-aware batch-compute scheduling market. The service will evolve around scheduling and migrating batch jobs using live energy mix, regional carbon intensity, execution cost, deadlines, and data-residency constraints.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	The initial public endpoint is `GET /health`, which returns JSON with `status: "ok"`.
14	
15	## Audit endpoint
16	
17	```bash
18	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN
19	```
20	
21	`--audit` and `--token` form a pair: both omitted leaves `GET /audit` a plain 404 like any other unknown path, while giving only one, an empty value or a repeated option is a usage error (exit status 2). When both are given, `GET /audit` serves read-only queries against the audit journal at `PATH`; clients cannot select another file.
22	
23	Requests must carry exactly one `X-Audit-Token` header whose value equals `TOKEN` (missing, blank or duplicated headers get 401, a mismatched value 403). The query string maps to `audit.search`: optional `cursor`, `limit` (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, default 100), `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. Unknown, repeated or empty parameters get 400 `invalid_request`. A missing journal gets 404 `audit_not_found`, malformed journal content 409 `audit_invalid`, and other I/O failures 503 `audit_unavailable`.
24	
25	## Multi-token scoped authorization
26	
27	```bash
28	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG
29	```
30	
31	`--auth` is an alternative to `--token`; the two are mutually exclusive, and enabling the audit endpoint requires exactly one of them (anything else is a usage error, exit status 2). `CONFIG` is a UTF-8 file whose every non-empty line is a six-element JSON array:
32	
33	```json
34	["name", "sha256-hex", grace_until, ops, stages, keys]
35	```
36	
37	- `name` — a unique non-empty label for the token.
38	- `sha256-hex` — the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the token's raw UTF-8 bytes; unique across records. The file never holds plaintext tokens.
39	- `grace_until` — `null` or a non-negative integer Unix second; the token stays valid while the current Unix second is not greater than it.
40	- `ops`, `stages`, `keys` — each either `"*"` (the filter may be omitted or take any legal value) or an array of distinct non-empty strings, in which case the request must carry that filter explicitly with a value in the array. Operation and stage scopes use the search filter domains (`copy`/`restore`; `成功`, `校验`, `执行`, `同步`, `回滚`); history keys match exactly.
41	
42	The whole file is validated at startup (any error exits with status 2 without listening) and re-read on every request, so a same-directory atomic replacement rotates tokens without a restart: add the new digest and set a grace cutoff on the old one. A configuration that cannot be read or validated after startup answers 503 `auth_unavailable`. Unknown or expired tokens get 403; a valid token whose request lacks a required in-scope filter gets 403 as well, after query-parameter validation (400) and before the audit file is ever opened.
43	
44	## Proof export endpoint
45	
46	```bash
47	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN --checkpoint CPATH
48	```
49	
50	`--checkpoint` enables `GET /audit/proof`, the online export of `audit_proof.export` against the fixed checkpoint `CPATH`; it may only be given together with `--audit` (alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error, exit status 2). Without it the proof path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path. Clients can never select the audit or checkpoint file through the query.
51	
52	The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order (401/403, 400 `invalid_request`, scoped filters 403, 503 `auth_unavailable`). The query takes a mandatory non-empty `generation` name, an optional `final` flag (exactly `true` or `false`, defaulting to `false`) and the usual `cursor`, `limit`, `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. A successful export answers 200 with the offline-savable proof object, its page computed from the same journal snapshot the proof seals. The proof object is version 2 and ends with `checkpoint_etag`: the strong entity tag of the checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint download serves — so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint snapshot, and any later anchor, closing or new generation rebinds the proofs that follow it. A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory gets 404 `proof_not_found` (the real paths never leak); an invalid chain, checkpoint, generation state or growth relation gets 409 `proof_invalid` and appends no anchor; locking or I/O failures get 503 `proof_unavailable` with the old checkpoint preserved.
53	
54	## Checkpoint snapshot endpoint
55	
56	With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.
57	
58	Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.
59	
60	The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.
61	
62	The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.
63	
64	## Offline bundle verification
65	
66	```bash
67	python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG [--trust-dir PATH]
68	```
69	
70	`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three mandatory options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.
71	
72	Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.
73	
74	The optional `--trust-dir PATH` keeps a persistent sequence of the snapshots this machine has accepted, so a whole-bundle replay of an older — otherwise self-consistent — pair is rejected as a rollback. Without the option the single-bundle verification above runs unchanged and no directory is created.
75	
76	The directory carries a lifecycle marker, `state.json`, that leaves exactly one explainable stage after any interruption. When the directory does not yet exist but its parent does, the first verification commits a `"preparing"` state first — binding the bundle's strong tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the candidate node digest — then saves the content-addressed snapshot and node and commits the chain head; the state advances to `"ready"` only after the head commit, and a ready record binds the head digest as well. An interruption in any of those windows is recovered idempotently: the same complete bundle resumes from `preparing` and finishes the sequence, while a bundle carrying a different tag or snapshot is rejected with every staged piece of evidence retained. An existing directory that contains neither a state nor a head — an empty directory, or one holding only unreferenced fragments — is never taken over. A directory from before the lifecycle existed (a legal chain head but no state) is adopted only after its whole chain verifies, and is then stamped ready.
77	
78	With it, the existing verification completes first; then, under the trust directory's exclusive lock, the retained sequence is inspected from its first node to its head on every call: each node digest is recomputed from its strong tag, predecessor tag, checkpoint digest and predecessor node digest; each predecessor digest is followed to a real node whose tag matches; every node's checkpoint snapshot must exist, hit its content address and pass the complete structure and anchor-chain validation; and each pair of adjacent snapshots must satisfy the strict append-only relation below — history continuity is never inferred from node metadata alone. A ready state must also bind the head, the head node and the current snapshot to one another; a missing head or a crosswise relation fails verification. A same-tag replay walks the whole chain just the same, so a corrupted historical node or snapshot cannot be masked by the current bundle. A later bundle carrying the head's strong tag is an idempotent replay: the proof is fully re-verified, the full chain is re-inspected and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the latest trusted one — existing generations, anchors, fields and values must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may be appended — so an already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors, or a bundle that cannot continue the head fails verification.
79	
80	Each sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks the real predecessor relation from disk; tampered node content, chain digests, snapshots or head relations are never repaired from the bundle in hand. Directory updates serialize across processes and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs, with the head committed before the ready state: any failure keeps the pre-call state, unreferenced complete files are reused on reentry, leftover fragments never take part in any decision, and a content address that already holds different bytes is never overwritten or repaired.
81	
82	On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding and malformed trust metadata), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, predecessor, snapshot, lifecycle-state, page, snapshot-binding or trust-sequence mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files, a missing trust-directory parent, or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.
83	
84	## Test
85	
86	```bash
87	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
88	```
89


`--checkpoint` enables `GET /audit/proof`, the online export of `audit_proof.export` against the fixed checkpoint `CPATH`; it may only be given together with `--audit` (alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error, exit status 2). Without it the proof path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path. Clients can never select the audit or checkpoint file through the query.

The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order (401/403, 400 `invalid_request`, scoped filters 403, 503 `auth_unavailable`). The query takes a mandatory non-empty `generation` name, an optional `final` flag (exactly `true` or `false`, defaulting to `false`) and the usual `cursor`, `limit`, `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. A successful export answers 200 with the offline-savable proof object, its page computed from the same journal snapshot the proof seals. The proof object is version 2 and ends with `checkpoint_etag`: the strong entity tag of the checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint download serves — so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint snapshot, and any later anchor, closing or new generation rebinds the proofs that follow it. A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory gets 404 `proof_not_found` (the real paths never leak); an invalid chain, checkpoint, generation state or growth relation gets 409 `proof_invalid` and appends no anchor; locking or I/O failures get 503 `proof_unavailable` with the old checkpoint preserved.

## Checkpoint snapshot endpoint

With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.

Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.

The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.

The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.

## Offline bundle verification

```bash
python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG [--trust-dir PATH]
```

`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three mandatory options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.

Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.

The optional `--trust-dir PATH` keeps a persistent sequence of the snapshots this machine has accepted, so a whole-bundle replay of an older — otherwise self-consistent — pair is rejected as a rollback. Without the option the single-bundle verification above runs unchanged and no directory is created.

The directory carries a lifecycle marker, `state.json`, that leaves exactly one explainable stage after any interruption. When the directory does not yet exist but its parent does, the first verification commits a `"preparing"` state first — binding the bundle's strong tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the candidate node digest — then saves the content-addressed snapshot and node and commits the chain head; the state advances to `"ready"` only after the head commit, and a ready record binds the head digest as well. An interruption in any of those windows is recovered idempotently: the same complete bundle resumes from `preparing` and finishes the sequence, while a bundle carrying a different tag or snapshot is rejected with every staged piece of evidence retained. An existing directory that contains neither a state nor a head — an empty directory, or one holding only unreferenced fragments — is never taken over. A directory from before the lifecycle existed (a legal chain head but no state) is adopted only after its whole chain verifies, and is then stamped ready.

With it, the existing verification completes first; then, under the trust directory's exclusive lock, the retained sequence is inspected from its first node to its head on every call: each node digest is recomputed from its strong tag, predecessor tag, checkpoint digest and predecessor node digest; each predecessor digest is followed to a real node whose tag matches; every node's checkpoint snapshot must exist, hit its content address and pass the complete structure and anchor-chain validation; and each pair of adjacent snapshots must satisfy the strict append-only relation below — history continuity is never inferred from node metadata alone. A ready state must also bind the head, the head node and the current snapshot to one another; a missing head or a crosswise relation fails verification. A same-tag replay walks the whole chain just the same, so a corrupted historical node or snapshot cannot be masked by the current bundle. A later bundle carrying the head's strong tag is an idempotent replay: the proof is fully re-verified, the full chain is re-inspected and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the latest trusted one — existing generations, anchors, fields and values must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may be appended — so an already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors, or a bundle that cannot continue the head fails verification.

Each sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks the real predecessor relation from disk; tampered node content, chain digests, snapshots or head relations are never repaired from the bundle in hand. Directory updates serialize across processes and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs, with the head committed before the ready state: any failure keeps the pre-call state, unreferenced complete files are reused on reentry, leftover fragments never take part in any decision, and a content address that already holds different bytes is never overwritten or repaired.

On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding and malformed trust metadata), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, predecessor, snapshot, lifecycle-state, page, snapshot-binding or trust-sequence mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files, a missing trust-directory parent, or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.

"""Offline verification of a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair.

Covers the ``verify-bundle`` command and the underlying
``audit_proof.verify_bundle``: the exactly-once non-empty argument
contract and the strong-tag format (usage errors that never read the
input files), the tag recomputation from the raw checkpoint bytes
before any parsing, the three-way agreement of the passed tag, the
recomputed tag and the proof's bound ``checkpoint_etag``, the
UTF-8/strict-JSON format checks of both files (version 1 proofs
without the snapshot binding are incomplete structures), the full
anchor-chain and proof cross-checks against one locked snapshot, the
compact single-line success and failure objects, and the
exit-status/error-code mapping (2 invalid_request, 3 invalid_bundle,
4 verification_failed, 5 bundle_unavailable).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import unittest
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest import mock

from carbon_market import audit, audit_proof
from carbon_market.__main__ import main


def _event(op: str = "copy", key: str = "batch-key",
           error: str | None = None, stage: str | None = None) -> dict:
    return {"op": op, "target": "t.history", "key": key,
            "changed": True, "error": error, "stage": stage}


def _run_cli(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    stdout = io.StringIO()
    stderr = io.StringIO()
    argv = ["carbon_market", "verify-bundle", *args]
    with mock.patch.object(sys, "argv", argv), \
            contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), \
            contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
        try:
            main()
            status = 0
        except SystemExit as exc:
            status = exc.code
    return status, stdout.getvalue(), stderr.getvalue()


class _Fixture(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.journal = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "audit.json")
        self.checkpoint = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "checkpoint.json")
        self.proof_path = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "proof.json")

    def _record(self, audit_key: str, **event_kwargs) -> None:
        audit.record(self.journal, audit_key, _event(**event_kwargs))

    def _export(self, generation: str = "g1", **kwargs) -> dict:
        proof = audit_proof.export(self.journal, self.checkpoint,
                                   generation, **kwargs)
        with open(self.proof_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(proof, ensure_ascii=False))
        return proof

    def _etag(self, path: str | None = None) -> str:
        with open(path or self.checkpoint, "rb") as handle:
            return '"' + hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest() + '"'

    def _write(self, path: str, raw: bytes) -> str:
        with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(raw)
        return '"' + hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() + '"'

    def _run(self, *args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        return _run_cli(*args)

    def _run_bundle(self, checkpoint: str | None = None,
                    proof: str | None = None,
                    etag: str | None = None) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        return self._run(
            "--checkpoint", checkpoint or self.checkpoint,
            "--proof", proof or self.proof_path,
            "--etag", etag if etag is not None else self._etag())


class SuccessTest(_Fixture):
    def test_valid_bundle_reports_verified_fields(self) -> None:
        self._record("b", error="OSError", stage="同步")
        self._record("a")
        self._record("c", error="OSError", stage="校验")
        proof = self._export("世代-1")
        # The proof binds the checkpoint snapshot it was exported from.
        self.assertEqual(proof["checkpoint_etag"], self._etag())
        status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle()
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertEqual(stderr, "")
        result = json.loads(stdout)
        self.assertEqual(list(result),
                         ["valid", "etag", "generation", "closed",
                          "events", "next"])
        self.assertIs(result["valid"], True)
        self.assertEqual(result["etag"], self._etag())
        self.assertEqual(result["generation"], "世代-1")
        self.assertIs(result["closed"], False)
        self.assertEqual([key for key, _ in result["events"]],
                         ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertIsNone(result["next"])
        # Compact UTF-8 JSON: Chinese written through, exactly one
        # trailing newline.
        self.assertIn("世代-1", stdout)
        self.assertIn("同步", stdout)
        self.assertNotIn("\\u", stdout)
        self.assertNotIn(": ", stdout)
        self.assertNotIn(", ", stdout)
        self.assertTrue(stdout.endswith("\n"))
        self.assertFalse(stdout.endswith("\n\n"))

    def test_page_and_cursor_come_from_the_verified_proof(self) -> None:
        for index in range(5):
            self._record(f"k{index}")
        proof = self._export(limit=2)
        status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle()
        self.assertEqual((status, stderr), (0, ""))
        result = json.loads(stdout)
        self.assertEqual(result["events"], proof["result"]["events"])
        self.assertEqual(result["next"], "k1")
        # The following page verifies against the same checkpoint.
        proof2 = audit_proof.export(self.journal, self.checkpoint, "g1",
                                    cursor="k1", limit=2)
        with open(self.proof_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(proof2, ensure_ascii=False))
        status, stdout, _ = self._run_bundle()
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        result = json.loads(stdout)
        self.assertEqual([key for key, _ in result["events"]],
                         ["k2", "k3"])
        self.assertEqual(result["next"], "k3")

    def test_closed_generation_reports_closed_true(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export("g1", final=True)
        status, stdout, _ = self._run_bundle()
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        result = json.loads(stdout)
        self.assertIs(result["closed"], True)

    def test_inputs_are_never_rewritten(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        before_checkpoint = open(self.checkpoint, "rb").read()
        before_proof = open(self.proof_path, "rb").read()
        self.assertEqual(self._run_bundle()[0], 0)
        self.assertEqual(open(self.checkpoint, "rb").read(),
                         before_checkpoint)
        self.assertEqual(open(self.proof_path, "rb").read(), before_proof)


class ArgumentTest(_Fixture):
    def test_missing_options_are_invalid_request(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        good = ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint,
                "--proof", self.proof_path,
                "--etag", self._etag()]
        for omit in (0, 2, 4):
            args = good[:omit] + good[omit + 2:]
            with self.subTest(omit=good[omit]):
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run(*args)
                self.assertEqual(status, 2)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_request"})

    def test_repeated_empty_and_unknown_arguments_are_invalid_request(
            self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        etag = self._etag()
        variants = [
            ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint, "--checkpoint",
             self.checkpoint, "--proof", self.proof_path, "--etag", etag],
            ["--checkpoint", "", "--proof", self.proof_path,
             "--etag", etag],
            ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint, "--proof", "",
             "--etag", etag],
            ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint, "--proof", self.proof_path,
             "--etag", ""],
            ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint, "--proof", self.proof_path,
             "--etag", etag, "--extra", "x"],
            ["--checkpoint", self.checkpoint, "--proof", self.proof_path,
             "--etag", etag, "positional"],
            ["--checkpoint"],  # option without a value
        ]
        for args in variants:
            with self.subTest(args=args):
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run(*args)
                self.assertEqual(status, 2)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_request"})

    def test_malformed_etags_are_invalid_request(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        good = hashlib.sha256(b"x").hexdigest()
        for etag in (
            f'"{good[:63]}"',                       # too short
            f'"{good}a"',                           # too long
            f'"{good.upper()}"',                    # uppercase
            f'"{"g" * 64}"',                        # not hexadecimal
            good,                                   # unquoted
            f'"{good}", "{good}"',                  # list
            "*",                                    # wildcard
            f'W/"{good}"',                          # weak tag
            f' "{good}"',                           # surrounding space
        ):
            with self.subTest(etag=etag):
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(etag=etag)
                self.assertEqual(status, 2)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_request"})

    def test_argument_errors_never_read_the_input_files(self) -> None:
        # Neither path exists; an argument error must win over any file
        # access, so the outcome is 2, never 5.
        missing = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "missing.json")
        for args in (
            ["--checkpoint", missing, "--proof", missing],
            ["--checkpoint", missing, "--proof", missing, "--etag", ""],
            ["--checkpoint", missing, "--proof", missing,
             "--etag", "not-a-tag"],
            ["--checkpoint", missing, "--proof", missing,
             "--etag", '"0" * 64"'],
        ):
            with self.subTest(args=args):
                status, _, stderr = self._run(*args)
                self.assertEqual(status, 2)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_request"})

    def test_library_rejects_bad_arguments_before_reading(self) -> None:
        missing = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "missing.json")
        for args in (("", "p", '"0"'), ("c", "", '"0"'), ("c", "p", ""),
                     ("c", "p", "unquoted"), (missing, missing, "x")):
            with self.subTest(args=args):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    audit_proof.verify_bundle(*args)


class UnavailableTest(_Fixture):
    def test_missing_files_are_bundle_unavailable(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        missing = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "missing.json")
        for checkpoint, proof in ((missing, self.proof_path),
                                  (self.checkpoint, missing),
                                  (missing, missing)):
            with self.subTest(checkpoint=checkpoint, proof=proof):
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(
                    checkpoint=checkpoint, proof=proof)
                self.assertEqual(status, 5)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "bundle_unavailable"})

    def test_other_io_errors_are_bundle_unavailable(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        # A directory opens with an OSError that is not
        # FileNotFoundError.
        status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(checkpoint=self.tmp.name)
        self.assertEqual(status, 5)
        self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                         {"error": "bundle_unavailable"})

    def test_failure_object_never_leaks_paths_or_content(self) -> None:
        status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(etag='"' + "0" * 64 + '"')
        self.assertEqual(status, 5)
        self.assertNotIn(self.tmp.name, stderr)
        self.assertNotIn("checkpoint", stderr)
        self.assertEqual(stderr.strip(), '{"error":"bundle_unavailable"}')


class InvalidBundleTest(_Fixture):
    def test_checkpoint_format_errors_are_invalid_bundle(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        proof = self._export()
        good = open(self.checkpoint, "rb").read()
        document = json.loads(good)
        variants = [
            b"\xff\xfe is not utf-8",
            b"{not json",
            b'"version":1,"generations":[]}',  # not an object
            good.replace(b'"version":1', b'"version":-0', 1),
            good.replace(b'"version":1', b'"version":NaN', 1),
            good.replace(b'"version":1', b'"version":Infinity', 1),
            good.replace(b'"version":1', b'"version":2', 1),
            json.dumps({"generations": document["generations"],
                        "version": 1}, ensure_ascii=False,
                       separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8"),
        ]
        for raw in variants:
            with self.subTest(raw=raw[:24]):
                etag = self._write(self.checkpoint, raw)
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(etag=etag)
                self.assertEqual(status, 3)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_bundle"})

    def test_proof_format_errors_are_invalid_bundle(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        proof = self._export()
        good = json.dumps(proof, ensure_ascii=False,
                          separators=(",", ":"))
        incomplete = dict(proof)
        del incomplete["closed"]
        unbound = dict(proof)
        del unbound["checkpoint_etag"]
        version_one = dict(unbound)
        version_one["version"] = 1
        bad_tag = dict(proof, checkpoint_etag=proof["checkpoint_etag"]
                       [1:-1])  # unquoted
        variants = [
            b"\xff\xfe",
            b"{not json",
            good.replace('"limit":100', '"limit":-0', 1).encode("utf-8"),
            good.replace('"limit":100', '"limit":NaN', 1).encode("utf-8"),
            json.dumps(incomplete, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
            good.replace('"limit":100', '"limit":0', 1).encode("utf-8"),
            # No snapshot binding: version 1 proofs and version 2
            # envelopes missing checkpoint_etag are incomplete
            # structures, and a tag that is not one quoted 64-digit
            # lowercase digest is malformed.
            json.dumps(version_one, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
            json.dumps(unbound, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
            json.dumps(bad_tag, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
        ]
        for raw in variants:
            with self.subTest(raw=raw[:24]):
                with open(self.proof_path, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(raw)
                status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle()
                self.assertEqual(status, 3)
                self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                                 {"error": "invalid_bundle"})


class VerificationFailedTest(_Fixture):
    def test_etag_mismatch_fails_before_anything_else(self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._export()
        other = '"' + "0" * 64 + '"'
        status, stdout, stderr = self._run_bundle(etag=other)
        self.assertEqual(status, 4)
        self.assertEqual(stdout, "")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                         {"error": "verification_failed"})
        # Even a checkpoint that is not valid JSON at all fails with the
        # tag mismatch first: the tag is recomputed from the raw bytes
        # before any parsing.
        raw = b"{not json"
        self._write(self.checkpoint, raw)
        status, _, stderr = self._run_bundle(etag=other)
        self.assertEqual(status, 4)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(stderr),
                         {"error": "verification_failed"})

    def test_checkpoint_chain_deviations_are_verification_failed(
            self) -> None:
        self._record("a")
        self._record("b")
        self._export("g1")
        audit_proof.export(self.journal, self.checkpoint, "g1", final=True)
        document = json.loads(open(self.checkpoint, encoding="utf-8")
                              .read())
        variants = []
        tampered = json.loads(json.dumps(document))
        tampered["generations"][-1]["anchors"][-1]["digest"] = "0" * 64
        variants.append(tampered)
        tampered = json.loads(json.dumps(document))
        tampered["generations"][-1]["anchors"][-1]["previous"] = "0" * 64
        variants.append(tampered)
        tampered = json.loads(json.dumps(document))

            except audit_proof.BundleMismatchError:

                # already anchored one, resealing its digest: the
                # export is cleanly rejected and appends nothing --
                # itself a self-consistent outcome.

            except BaseException as exc:  # pragma: no cover

                        # read no longer saw, or an export rebound the
                        # checkpoint after the proof was written: a
                        # complete old or new combination, never a torn
                        # one.
                        outcomes.append("mismatch")
                    else:

                        outcomes.append("valid")

        for thread in threads:

        self.assertTrue(outcomes)

1	"""Independent checkpoints and scope proofs over the audit journal.
2	
3	This module adds two capabilities the read-only :mod:`carbon_market.audit`
4	journal does not provide on its own: an independent checkpoint file that
5	is not the journal and an offline-savable proof of a particular search.
6	
7	:func:`export` reads the complete journal snapshot under the *same*
8	``cursor`` / ``limit`` / ``op`` / ``stage`` / ``key`` arguments
9	:func:`carbon_market.audit.search` takes and returns a version 2 proof
10	object that encapsulates the query, the result page and the journal's
11	raw bytes, together with the named generation and its closed state. The
12	proof ends with ``checkpoint_etag``: the strong entity tag of the
13	checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- one
14	double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of
15	the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint
16	download serves -- so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint
17	snapshot. Each successful non-duplicate export appends one anchor to
18	the checkpoint at ``checkpoint_path``: the anchor binds
19	
20	* the complete event manifest -- every audit key paired with its event
21	  digest, in journal order;
22	* the SHA-256 of the journal's raw bytes (the *log digest*), so a log
23	  rotation that preserves the sealed events still produces a new anchor
24	  while the chain continues;
25	* the root head the journal declares;
26	* the digest of the previous anchor (null for the very first anchor of
27	  the checkpoint, so the stream stays one continuous chain across
28	  generations) and the closed flag.
29	
30	The query parameters and the returned page are not anchored: the proof
31	carries them and :func:`verify` recomputes the page from the embedded
32	journal bytes and parameters, so any tampering with log bytes,
33	parameters, page or cursor shows up as a mismatch. Exports of different
34	queries against an unchanged snapshot append no anchor; their proofs
35	name the snapshot's existing anchor.
36	
37	The anchor digest is the SHA-256 of that five-part binding serialized with the
38	journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention, so rotating the journal bytes
39	while the sealed chain survives keeps the anchor chain continuous --
40	every anchor also commits to the previous anchor digest.
41	
42	Generations are non-empty, unique, non-regressing names (strictly
43	ascending in code-point order): a checkpoint is an ordered list of
44	generations, and a new generation can only be created once the previous
45	one is closed. Within one generation every export must
46	preserve the already anchored events key by key and digest by digest; a
47	snapshot may keep the same manifest (a re-query, or a byte-preserving
48	log rotation) or add new keys -- which may land anywhere in code-point
49	order, since the anchored pairs are compared key by key, not by
50	position -- but a deletion, a rewrite of a known event or a retreat
51	raises ``ValueError`` and appends nothing. An export
52	identical in manifest, log digest, head and closed state is a duplicate:
53	it appends no anchor and returns a proof naming that same anchor, no
54	matter which query it carried. Passing ``final=True`` closes the current
55	generation -- the closing anchor may pin the same snapshot, only its
56	closed flag flips -- and once closed only the identical idempotent
57	export (``final=True``) is accepted.
58	
59	:func:`verify` takes *only* the checkpoint path and a previously
60	exported proof -- the journal itself is never opened -- rechecks the
61	proof envelope, recomputes the strong tag of the checkpoint bytes read
62	under the lock and confronts it with the proof's bound
63	``checkpoint_etag``, recomputes the page from the embedded log bytes and
64	page, reparses the embedded journal, rechecks every anchor chain, and
65	returns the proof's original search result together with its generation
66	and closed state. Any change to the embedded log bytes, parameters, page
67	content, cursor or any digest raises ``ValueError``; a proof whose bound
68	tag does not match the checkpoint in hand -- an old proof against a new
69	checkpoint or a new proof against an old one -- mismatches as well.
70	
71	:func:`verify_bundle` is the offline entry for a downloaded pair: it
72	takes the checkpoint file, the saved proof file and the strong entity
73	tag the download carried, recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw
74	bytes before anything else, and then applies the same checkpoint and
75	proof validation as :func:`verify` against the single locked snapshot
76	it read, so a racing same-directory replacement can only yield a
77	self-consistent old or new combination. The passed tag, the recomputed
78	tag and the proof's bound ``checkpoint_etag`` must all three agree, so
79	a tag carried by another download response never verifies. Structural
80	failures (encoding, JSON grammar, field shapes, and version 1 proofs,
81	which predate the snapshot binding) raise ``BundleFormatError`` while
82	every tag, digest-chain, generation, anchor, closed-state, page or
83	snapshot-binding mismatch raises ``BundleMismatchError``; both are
84	public ``ValueError`` subclasses that let the command-line entry tell a
85	malformed bundle apart from a failed verification.
86	
87	:func:`verify_bundle` also accepts an optional *trust_dir*: a directory
88	holding a persistent sequence of snapshot nodes that lets this machine
89	reject a whole-bundle replay of an older, otherwise self-consistent
90	pair. With a trust directory the single-bundle verification runs first,
91	unchanged; then, under the trust directory's own exclusive lock, the
92	verified snapshot is compared with the retained chain head.
93	
94	The directory carries a lifecycle marker, ``state.json``, that makes
95	every on-disk stage uniquely explainable after an interruption. The
96	first verification of a not-yet-existing directory (whose parent
97	exists) commits a ``"preparing"`` state first -- binding the
98	candidate's strong tag, checkpoint byte digest and candidate node
99	digest -- then saves the content-addressed snapshot and node and
100	commits the chain head, and only after the head flips the state to
101	``"ready"`` (which additionally binds the head node digest). A crash
102	in any of those windows is resumed idempotently: the identical bundle
103	completes the preparation, while a different bundle is rejected with
104	every piece of evidence retained. A ``"ready"`` state is trusted only
105	after the head it names, the head node and the head snapshot are all
106	re-checked against one another. An existing directory that has neither
107	state nor head -- an empty directory or one holding only unreferenced
108	fragments -- is never taken over, and a directory from before the
109	lifecycle existed (a legal head but no state) is adopted only after
110	its whole chain verifies, then stamped ready.
111	
112	Every verification walks the retained chain from its first node to the
113	head: each node digest is recomputed over tag, predecessor tag,
114	checkpoint digest and predecessor node digest, each predecessor
115	relation is followed to a real node, each checkpoint snapshot must
116	exist, hit its content address and pass the complete structure and
117	anchor-chain validation, and each pair of adjacent snapshots must
118	satisfy the strict append-only relation -- history continuity is never
119	inferred from node metadata alone. A same-tag replay walks the whole
120	chain as well, so any corrupted historical node or snapshot fails
121	instead of being masked by the current bundle. Unreferenced fragments
122	are left untouched and never take part in a decision; a content
123	address that already holds different bytes is never overwritten or
124	repaired.
125	
126	A later bundle carrying the same strong tag is an idempotent replay:
127	the proof is fully re-verified, the retained chain is fully
128	re-inspected and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted
129	only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the
130	latest trusted one -- existing generations, anchors, fields and values
131	must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may follow. An
132	already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors or a
133	bundle that cannot continue the head is rejected as a rollback. Every
134	sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the
135	checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head
136	points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks
137	the real predecessor relation from disk. Tampered node content, chain
138	digests, snapshots or head relations are never repaired from the
139	bundle in hand: the evidence stays and the verification fails.
140	Directory updates serialize across processes, commit through
141	same-directory temporary files, fsync, atomic replace and directory
142	fsyncs, and the head is always committed before the ready state, so any
143	failure keeps the pre-call state; unreferenced complete files are
144	reused on reentry and leftover fragments never take part in any
145	decision. Trust metadata that is not valid UTF-8/JSON, carries a
146	negative-zero literal, or breaks field order, version or structure
147	raises ``BundleFormatError``; a chain digest, snapshot, predecessor,
148	head or lifecycle-state mismatch, an old-version replay or a forked
149	continuation raises ``BundleMismatchError``; a missing trust-directory
150	parent raises ``FileNotFoundError`` and every other locking or I/O
151	failure surfaces as ``OSError``.
152	
153	Exports only accept a complete version 2 journal: a version 1 journal,
154	a broken digest chain or a malformed checkpoint structure raises
155	``ValueError``. Invalid argument types, an empty generation name, a
156	non-boolean ``final`` or out-of-range search parameters are rejected
157	with ``ValueError`` *before any file is read*. A missing audit journal,
158	a checkpoint required for verification, or a missing checkpoint parent
159	directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; every other locking or I/O
160	failure surfaces unchanged as ``OSError``.
161	
162	An export holds the journal's shared kernel flock and the checkpoint's
163	exclusive kernel flock together, and the checkpoint commits via a
164	same-directory temporary file that is written and fsynced, moved over
165	the checkpoint with :func:`os.replace` and followed by a directory
166	fsync. A commit failure therefore never leaves a new anchor behind nor
167	returns a proof; concurrent appenders serialize and each observes
168	either the complete previous checkpoint or the complete new one, and a
169	restarted process continues the same anchor chain from the persisted
170	checkpoint.
171	"""

366	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2 \
367	                or not isinstance(item[0], str) or not item[0] \
368	                or not _is_digest(item[1]):
369	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest entries must be "
370	                                    "[non-empty key, 64-digit hex digest]")
371	        if last_key is not None and item[0] <= last_key:
372	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be ordered by "
373	                                    "key code point without repeats")
374	        manifest.append([item[0], item[1]])
375	        last_key = item[0]
376	    return manifest

379	def _check_extension(old_manifest: list[list[Any]],
380	                     new_manifest: list[list[Any]]) -> None:
381	    # The old snapshot must survive key by key: every anchored key keeps
382	    # its exact digest, while new keys may land anywhere in code-point
383	    # order -- the manifests are compared as key/digest pairs, not by
384	    # position. Fewer entries (retreat), a missing old key (deletion) or
385	    # a changed digest under a known key (rewrite) all surface here.
386	    # Equal manifests (re-query or byte-level log rotation with same
387	    # events) are permitted by the caller and never reach this check.
388	    if len(new_manifest) <= len(old_manifest):
389	        raise BundleMismatchError("a generation only accepts snapshots "
390	                                  "that add new audit events")
391	    new_digests = {audit_key: digest for audit_key, digest in new_manifest}
392	    for audit_key, digest in old_manifest:
393	        if new_digests.get(audit_key) != digest:
394	            raise BundleMismatchError("a generation cannot rewrite, delete "
395	                                      "or reorder an already anchored event")
396

398	def _validate_checkpoint(data: object) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
399	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
400	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint root must be an object with "
401	                                "keys version and generations, in that "
402	                                "order")
403	    version = data["version"]
404	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
405	            or version != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
406	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported checkpoint version")
407	    generations_raw = data["generations"]
408	    if not isinstance(generations_raw, list):
409	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint generations must be a list")
410	    if not generations_raw:
411	        # export only creates a checkpoint together with its first
412	        # generation, so a persisted empty list is structural damage.
413	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint must carry at least one "
414	                                "generation")
415	
416	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
417	    generations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
418	    # The previous-anchor chain runs across the whole checkpoint: the
419	    # first anchor of a later generation names the last anchor of the
420	    # closed previous generation, so the stream never forks.
421	    previous: str | None = None
422	    for gen_position, generation_raw in enumerate(generations_raw):
423	        is_last_generation = gen_position == len(generations_raw) - 1
424	        if not isinstance(generation_raw, dict) \
425	                or list(generation_raw.keys()) != list(_GENERATION_FIELDS):
426	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must be an object "
427	                                    "with keys name and anchors, in that "
428	                                    "order")
429	        name = generation_raw["name"]
430	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
431	            raise BundleFormatError("generation name must be a non-empty "
432	                                    "string")
433	        if name in seen_names:
434	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not repeat")
435	        if generations and name <= generations[-1]["name"]:
436	            # Names open in strictly ascending code-point order; an
437	            # equal-or-earlier name is a repeat or a regression.
438	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not regress")
439	        seen_names.add(name)
440	        anchors_raw = generation_raw["anchors"]
441	        if not isinstance(anchors_raw, list) or not anchors_raw:
442	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must carry at least "
443	                                    "one anchor")
444	
445	        anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
446	        for index, anchor_raw in enumerate(anchors_raw):
447	            is_last_anchor = index == len(anchors_raw) - 1
448	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw, dict) \
449	                    or list(anchor_raw.keys()) != list(_ANCHOR_FIELDS):
450	                raise BundleFormatError(
451	                    "each anchor must be an object with keys manifest, "
452	                    "log_digest, head, previous, closed and digest, in "
453	                    "that order")
454	            manifest = _validate_manifest(anchor_raw["manifest"])
455	            if not _is_digest(anchor_raw["log_digest"]):
456	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor log_digest must be a "
457	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
458	                                        "digest")
459	            head = anchor_raw["head"]
460	            if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
461	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor head must be null or a "
462	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
463	                                        "digest")
464	            declared_previous = anchor_raw["previous"]
465	            if index > 0 and not _is_digest(declared_previous):
466	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor previous digest must be a "
467	                                        "64-digit hexadecimal digest")
468	            if declared_previous != previous:
469	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor previous digest does not "
470	                                          "continue the chain")
471	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw["closed"], bool):
472	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor closed must be a boolean")
473	            digest = anchor_raw["digest"]
474	            if not _is_digest(digest):
475	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor digest must be a 64-digit "
476	                                        "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
477	            expected = _anchor_digest(manifest, anchor_raw["log_digest"],
478	                                      head, previous, anchor_raw["closed"])
479	            if digest != expected:
480	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor digest does not match "
481	                                          "its content")
482	
483	            if anchors:
484	                earlier = anchors[-1]
485	                if earlier["closed"]:
486	                    raise BundleMismatchError("a closed anchor cannot be "
487	                                              "followed inside its "
488	                                              "generation")
489	                # Consecutive anchors either pin the same manifest (a
490	                # byte-level log rotation with the events intact, or the
491	                # closing anchor flipping the closed flag) or extend it
492	                # with new keys anywhere in code-point order while every
493	                # anchored pair survives; anything else is a rewrite.
494	                if manifest == earlier["manifest"]:
495	                    if head != earlier["head"]:
496	                        raise BundleMismatchError(
497	                            "a same-snapshot anchor cannot move the root "
498	                            "digest")
499	                    if anchor_raw["log_digest"] == earlier["log_digest"] \
500	                            and anchor_raw["closed"] == earlier["closed"]:
501	                        raise BundleMismatchError("a duplicate anchor "
502	                                                  "changes nothing")
503	                else:
504	                    _check_extension(earlier["manifest"], manifest)
505	            if anchor_raw["closed"] and not is_last_anchor:
506	                raise BundleMismatchError("only the last anchor of a "
507	                                          "generation may be closed")
508	
509	            anchor = {"manifest": manifest,
510	                      "log_digest": anchor_raw["log_digest"], "head": head,
511	                      "previous": declared_previous,
512	                      "closed": anchor_raw["closed"], "digest": digest}
513	            anchors.append(anchor)
514	            previous = digest
515	
516	        if not is_last_generation and not anchors[-1]["closed"]:
517	            # An open generation may only be the last one of the
518	            # checkpoint: any following generation proves it was closed.
519	            raise BundleMismatchError("a new generation can only start "
520	                                      "after the previous one is closed")
521	        generations.append({"name": name, "anchors": anchors})
522	    return generations

555	def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
556	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
557	    try:
558	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
559	    finally:

563	def _commit_checkpoint(realpath: str, directory: str, payload: bytes,
564	                       old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
565	    # Same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync --
566	    # with a rollback if anything fails after the replace, so a failed
567	    # commit never leaves the new anchor behind. The pre-call bytes are
568	    # staged back over the file (or the file removed when it did not
569	    # exist) and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive
570	    # lock is held; a failed rollback surfaces chained after the first
571	    # error.
572	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
573	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-proof-", suffix=".tmp")
574	    try:
575	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
576	            handle.write(payload)
577	            handle.flush()
578	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
579	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
580	    except BaseException as first:
581	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
582	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
583	        raise
584	    try:
585	        _fsync_dir(directory)
586	    except BaseException as first:
587	        audit._rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
588	        raise

622	def export(
623	    audit_path: str,
624	    checkpoint_path: str,
625	    generation: str,
626	    final: bool = False,
627	    cursor: str | None = None,
628	    limit: int = audit._DEFAULT_LIMIT,
629	    op: str | None = None,
630	    stage: str | None = None,
631	    key: str | None = None,
632	) -> dict[str, Any]:
633	    """Export a verifiable proof and anchor it in the checkpoint.
634	
635	    ``audit_path`` and ``checkpoint_path`` must be non-empty strings;
636	    ``generation`` must be a non-empty string and ``final`` a boolean.
637	    The search arguments follow :func:`carbon_market.audit.search`. All
638	    argument errors raise ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
639	
640	    A missing audit journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; so does a
641	    missing parent directory of a checkpoint that must be created. A
642	    version 1 journal, an incomplete digest chain, a malformed
643	    checkpoint, a repeated generation name or an export that reopens a
644	    past generation, an attempt to open a new generation while the
645	    previous one is still open, an export that deletes or rewrites
646	    events of the current generation, or any non-identical export of a
647	    closed generation raises ``ValueError``. Remaining locking or I/O
648	    failures raise ``OSError``.
649	
650	    Returns the offline proof dict: a version 2 envelope whose last
651	    field, ``checkpoint_etag``, is the strong entity tag of the
652	    checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- the same
653	    quoted SHA-256 the checkpoint download serves. A repeat of an export
654	    whose content and closed state are identical appends nothing and
655	    returns a proof naming the same anchor and the unchanged snapshot's
656	    tag. With ``final=True`` the appended anchor closes
657	    generation -- it may pin the same snapshot -- after which only the
658	    identical idempotent export (``final=True``) is accepted.
659	    """
660	    for value in (audit_path, checkpoint_path):
661	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
662	            raise ValueError("audit_path and checkpoint_path must be "
663	                             "non-empty strings")
664	    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not generation:
665	        raise ValueError("generation must be a non-empty string")
666	    if not isinstance(final, bool):
667	        raise ValueError("final must be a boolean")
668	    _check_params(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
669	
670	    audit_real = os.path.realpath(audit_path)
671	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
672	    checkpoint_store = _get_store(checkpoint_real)
673	    with checkpoint_store.lock:
674	        # Hold the journal's shared lock and the checkpoint's exclusive
675	        # lock together until the commit lands, so audit.record cannot
676	        # rotate the journal while its bytes are sealed into an anchor.
677	        with audit._file_lock(audit_real, shared=True):
678	            # Read inside the shared flock exactly like the read-only
679	            # audit queries: a racing audit.record is observed as one
680	            # complete document or the other, never a half-replaced
681	            # file. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError.
682	            with open(audit_real, "rb") as handle:
683	                raw = handle.read()
684	            document = _parse_journal_snapshot(audit_real, raw)
685	            with _file_lock(checkpoint_real):
686	                generations, old_bytes = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
687	                if generations is None:
688	                    generations = []
689	
690	                params = _params_dict(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
691	                # Compute the page from the exact bytes in hand; this is
692	                # the same filter/pagination audit.search applies.
693	                result = _search_document(document, params)
694	                manifest = _manifest(document)
695	                head = document["head"]
696	                log_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
697	                names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
698	
699	                def identical(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
700	                    return (item["manifest"] == manifest
701	                            and item["log_digest"] == log_digest
702	                            and item["head"] == head)
703	
704	                if generation in names:
705	                    position = names.index(generation)
706	                    if position != len(generations) - 1:
707	                        # A past generation can never be reopened.
708	                        raise ValueError("a past generation cannot be "
709	                                         "exported again")
710	                    current = generations[position]
711	                    anchors = current["anchors"]
712	                    last = anchors[-1]
713	
714	                    if last["closed"]:
715	                        # Once closed the only accepted export is the
716	                        # idempotent one: final stays true and the
717	                        # snapshot is byte-for-byte the same -- events,
718	                        # log bytes and root head. The query may differ,
719	                        # since verify recomputes the page from the
720	                        # embedded log and parameters.
721	                        if not final or not identical(last):
722	                            raise ValueError("a closed generation only "
723	                                             "accepts the identical "
724	                                             "idempotent export")
725	                        return _build_proof(
726	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
727	                            head, True, last["digest"],
728	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
729	
730	                    # Still open. Same events, same bytes, same head and
731	                    # not closing: the duplicate export appends nothing
732	                    # and returns the proof of the latest anchor. The
733	                    # manifest must equal the latest anchor's, so an
734	                    # older snapshot cannot mask a retreat.
735	                    if not final and manifest == last["manifest"] \
736	                            and identical(last):
737	                        return _build_proof(
738	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
739	                            head, False, last["digest"],
740	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
741	
742	                    # Otherwise append: the manifest grows (strict
743	                    # extension), stays identical with rotated log
744	                    # bytes, or stays identical while final flips the
745	                    # closed flag. A smaller or rewritten manifest is
746	                    # rejected.
747	                    if manifest != last["manifest"]:
748	                        _check_extension(last["manifest"], manifest)
749	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
750	                                              last["digest"], final)
751	                    anchors.append(new_anchor)
752	                else:
753	                    if generations and not \
754	                            generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["closed"]:
755	                        raise ValueError("a new generation can only be "
756	                                         "started after the previous one "
757	                                         "is closed")
758	                    if generations and generation <= generations[-1]["name"]:
759	                        raise ValueError("generation names must not "
760	                                         "regress")
761	                    previous_digest = (
762	                        None if not generations
763	                        else generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["digest"])
764	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
765	                                              previous_digest, final)
766	                    generations.append(
767	                        {"name": generation, "anchors": [new_anchor]})
768	
769	                payload = _serialize_checkpoint(generations)
770	                _commit_checkpoint(
771	                    checkpoint_real,
772	                    os.path.dirname(checkpoint_real) or ".",
773	                    payload, old_bytes)
774	                # The proof binds the snapshot just committed: while the
775	                # exclusive lock is held the on-disk bytes are exactly
776	                # the committed payload, so its tag is the one a
777	                # download of this checkpoint would serve.
778	                return _build_proof(generation, params, result, raw,
779	                                    log_digest, head, final,
780	                                    new_anchor["digest"],
781	                                    _strong_tag(payload))

786	        raise BundleFormatError("proof must be an object with the "
787	                                "exported fields in their original order")
788	    if not isinstance(data["version"], int) \
789	            or isinstance(data["version"], bool) \
790	            or data["version"] != _PROOF_VERSION:
791	        # A version 1 proof predates the checkpoint snapshot binding and
792	        # is treated as an incomplete proof structure, never as a
793	        # mismatch.
794	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported proof version")
795	    if not isinstance(data["generation"], str) or not data["generation"]:
796	        raise BundleFormatError("proof generation must be a non-empty "
797	                                "string")
798	    params = data["params"]
799	    if not isinstance(params, dict) \
800	            or list(params.keys()) != list(_PARAM_FIELDS):
801	        raise BundleFormatError("proof params must be the exported query "
802	                                "parameters")
803	    try:
804	        _check_params(params["cursor"], params["limit"], params["op"],
805	                      params["stage"], params["key"])
806	    except ValueError as exc:
807	        raise BundleFormatError(str(exc)) from exc
808	    result = data["result"]
809	    if not isinstance(result, dict) \
810	            or list(result.keys()) != ["events", "next"]:
811	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result must be the exported search "
812	                                "result")
813	    if not isinstance(result["events"], list):
814	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result events must be a list")
815	    next_cursor = result["next"]
816	    if next_cursor is not None and (not isinstance(next_cursor, str)
817	                                    or not next_cursor):
818	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result next must be null or a "
819	                                "non-empty string")
820	    if not isinstance(data["log_bytes"], str):
821	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_bytes must be a string")
822	    if not _is_digest(data["log_digest"]):
823	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_digest must be a 64-digit "
824	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
825	    head = data["head"]
826	    if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
827	        raise BundleFormatError("proof head must be null or a 64-digit "
828	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
829	    if not isinstance(data["closed"], bool):
830	        raise BundleFormatError("proof closed must be a boolean")
831	    if not _is_digest(data["anchor_digest"]):
832	        raise BundleFormatError("proof anchor_digest must be a 64-digit "
833	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
834	    checkpoint_etag = data["checkpoint_etag"]
835	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_etag, str) \
836	            or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_etag):
837	        raise BundleFormatError("proof checkpoint_etag must be a single "
838	                                "strong tag: a quoted 64-digit lowercase "
839	                                "hexadecimal digest")
840	    return data

843	def _search_document(document: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) \
844	        -> dict[str, Any]:
845	    # Recompute audit.search's result from an in-memory document so
846	    # verify never needs the journal file itself.
847	    cursor = params["cursor"]
848	    limit = params["limit"]
849	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
850	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
851	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
852	            continue
853	        if not audit._matches(event, params["op"], params["stage"],
854	                              params["key"]):
855	            continue
856	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
857	        if len(matches) > limit:
858	            break
859	    if len(matches) > limit:
860	        page = matches[:limit]
861	        return {"events": page, "next": page[-1][0]}
862	    return {"events": matches, "next": None}

865	def _verify_proof(generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
866	                  clean: dict[str, Any],
867	                  checkpoint_real: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
868	    # The cross-checks every verified proof must pass against one
869	    # checkpoint snapshot: the named generation and anchor must be
870	    # recorded, the embedded log bytes must hash to the anchored log
871	    # digest and reparse as a sealed version 2 journal whose manifest
872	    # and root head the anchor pins, and the page must recompute from
873	    # the embedded log and parameters. Every failure here is a
874	    # mismatch, never a format error.
875	    names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
876	    if clean["generation"] not in names:
877	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof generation is not recorded in "
878	                                  "the checkpoint")
879	    generation = generations[names.index(clean["generation"])]
880	    anchor = next((item for item in generation["anchors"]
881	                   if item["digest"] == clean["anchor_digest"]), None)
882	    if anchor is None:
883	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof anchor is not recorded in the "
884	                                  "checkpoint")
885	
886	    params = clean["params"]
887	    raw = clean["log_bytes"].encode("utf-8")
888	    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != clean["log_digest"]:
889	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log bytes do not match their "
890	                                  "log digest")
891	    if clean["log_digest"] != anchor["log_digest"]:
892	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log digest is not bound to the "
893	                                  "anchor")
894	    try:
895	        document = audit._parse_document(checkpoint_real, raw)
896	        audit._ensure_chain(document)
897	    except ValueError as exc:
898	        raise BundleMismatchError(str(exc)) from exc
899	    if document["version"] != 2:
900	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof requires a sealed version 2 "
901	                                  "audit journal")
902	    if clean["head"] != document["head"] \
903	            or anchor["head"] != document["head"]:
904	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof root digest does not match the "
905	                                  "journal")
906	    if _manifest(document) != anchor["manifest"]:
907	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof event manifest does not match "
908	                                  "the anchor")
909	    if clean["closed"] != anchor["closed"]:
910	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof closed state does not match "
911	                                  "the anchor")

913	    recomputed = _search_document(document, params)
914	    if recomputed != clean["result"]:
915	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof result does not follow from "
916	                                  "the embedded log and parameters")

918	            "next": clean["result"]["next"],
919	            "generation": clean["generation"],
920	            "closed": anchor["closed"]}
